title: Navy band clarinet section and getting discharged sick
summary: Purnell names the clarinet section, recalls playing in California, and tells of being discharged after the war while sick with high blood pressure.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Oh yeah, you had to read. In the Navy. That guy who was not Willie Helmford, he played first clarinet with us. In the Navy. I played second. A little boy called Old Joseph, you know him? Yeah. Old Joseph, he played solo clarinet.
And Tom played third. Yeah, that's right.
I mean Tom? Tom, Tom, Tom.

That was your brother. That was a good band. Now when I was in California with that band, Alvin played first, I played second. Just the time he went away, I played first parts of the marches. And then it took sick. After that, I had to play one night. He played one night in the dance band. See? And I was doing pretty good. After the war was over, everybody go over there. I had enough points, because my age was way up there. See? I went over there. Three months past, I'm going to ask the man. So I'm going to get out of there. I was the first one that went over there. He'd get examined to get out. Then after all that, when I get out, they didn't want to leave me out. I said, mm-mm-mm. After all that, when I get there, Max, you look at me. You got the rest, boy. I ain't made no money or nothing. Nothing wasn't hurting me. But I was sick then. I had that name. I had blood pressure. But they didn't tell me. They just told me you had the rest. I said, man, ain't nothing hurting me. He said, man, I can rest at my house. Come right out the neighbor and start waking. Then I was going every night. That's right.
